clue.text: Persian vessel under sail?

parts.note: a Persian is a long-haired breed of cat
a vessel is a boat

explanation.surface: A ship from Persia making its way across the sea under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, with the question mark admitting that a cat aboard a boat is a playful way to describe the craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A catboat is a small sailing craft with a single mast set well forward, so it is indeed a vessel driven by sail.

clue.text: Go against state to stage long-distance event

parts.note: to cross someone is to go against them
a state is a nation or country
to stage a show is to run it

explanation.surface: Someone defies the government in order to organise a big endurance race.
explanation.definitionFit: This race is run over open fields and hills rather than a track, typically covering many miles, so it is an endurance contest.

clue.text: Make record of socialist coming to a point

parts.note: to tape something is to make a recording of it
a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a log of a left-wing activist who is getting to the heart of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually toward one end until it reaches a tip, like a candle or spire.

clue.text: Remove from spurious throne

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow, lying across the gap between them

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A call to depose a pretender sitting on a throne he has no right to.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out of a position or office, which is to remove them.

clue.text: It's made to grasp torn net caught in broken cleat

indicators.note: something caught in a thing is held within it, so one group sits inside the other
a torn net has its strands pulled apart, so its letters are rearranged
a broken object is in pieces, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: the three letters of net in a new order
the five letters of cleat in a new order, opened after its first letter to take the other piece

explanation.surface: A fishing scene: a ripped net snagged on a damaged cleat on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled net goes inside the jumbled cleat after its first T, giving TENTACLE. A cleat is a fitting for tying a rope to.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus or squid uses its long flexible arms to seize prey, so each one is built for gripping things.

clue.text: There's method in loans for pedestrian tunnels

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, so its letters go inside

parts.note: subs are advances or loans, as of wages
a method is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A banker insists there is a system behind the lending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's method in' echoes 'there's method in his madness'. In Britain a subway is an underpass for walkers, not an underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage these are underground passages that let walkers cross beneath a busy road safely.

clue.text: Withdraw from middle of desert and surrender

indicators.note: only the central part of the word is kept, its two centre letters

parts.note: the two central letters of desert
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: A beleaguered army pulls back from the heart of the desert and gives in.
explanation.definitionFit: When a region secedes it formally breaks away from a federation or union, withdrawing its membership.

clue.text: Obscene killing, or rowdy commotion?

parts.note: blue jokes or films are obscene
a murder is an unlawful killing

explanation.surface: A tabloid wonders whether a lurid crime was a sordid homicide or just a noisy brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: To scream blue murder is a British idiom for making a great noisy fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a loud outcry or racket, as in 'yelling blue murder', a noisy uproar of protest.

clue.text: Magazine of famous London club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a store for weapons and ammunition
second meaning: a football club in north London

explanation.surface: The house periodical of a celebrated London gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' and 'club' suggest a publication and a members' club; really one is an arms store and the other is a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a military store of arms, and it is also the name of a well-known Premier League football side.

clue.text: Choice panel, part of parliamentary structure

parts.note: choice and select both mean picked out as the best
a panel is a committee of people

explanation.surface: An elite panel described as one piece of the machinery of Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: In Westminster these small groups of MPs or peers scrutinise government departments, forming one component of how Parliament works.

clue.text: Unusually nice pop solo sung by adversary in court

indicators.note: unusually means in an unaccustomed way, so the following letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these four words rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant pop song performed solo by someone's rival in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the barrister acting for the other side in a case, the lawyer who argues against you before the judge.

clue.text: Servant Caesar killed for hiding his tunic

parts.note: surface padding: it sets the scene and gives no letters

indicators.note: the earlier words conceal the letters inside them, keeping them out of sight

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A servant murdered Caesar to conceal the emperor's garment.
explanation.walkthrough: A sark is an old Scots word for a shirt or long tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect this word names a shirt or loose smock, which is a simple tunic-style garment.

clue.text: Uproarious terror grips extra-hard worker

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it inside one's grasp

parts.note: panic is sudden terror
a demon for work is someone who labours tirelessly

explanation.surface: A wild scene of fright takes hold of a workaholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandemonium is wild noisy chaos, and its adjective describes something marked by loud disorder and tumult.

clue.text: Drag a scout clumsily to marine safety unit

indicators.note: done clumsily means done awkwardly and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly hauls a Boy Scout off to the lifeboat station.
explanation.definitionFit: This service patrols shores and sea lanes, rescuing people in danger at sea and watching for hazards.

clue.text: Of a bygone era in which America took no part

definitions.text: in which America took no part
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the continents known before the voyages to the Americas

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like a history of some event the United States sat out, but it describes Europe, Asia and Africa, the hemisphere that excludes the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes quaint charm from times past, and also names the Eastern Hemisphere, which leaves out the Americas.

clue.text: Abstract reflections teens ditched for high jinks

indicators.note: abstract art breaks up its subject into rearranged shapes, so the remaining letters are reordered
these five letters are thrown away from the longer word

parts.note: the word taken as written before letters are removed
the letters to strip out of the longer word

explanation.surface: Deep thoughts are abandoned by youngsters in favour of horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T, E, E, N and S out of REFLECTIONS to leave R, F, L, C, I, O, then rearrange them. 'Abstract reflections' looks like a phrase about philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a bout of playful lively fun, much the same as boisterous high spirits or high jinks.

clue.text: Strong-arm man among men, for certain he's …

indicators.note: something among a group sits inside it, here inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spanning the three words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A heavy among a gang is surely, the clue continues, a man of solid build.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry the sentence into 17-down; the clue's own sense is complete before them.
explanation.definitionFit: An enforcer is a heavy employed to impose someone's will through threats or violence, a muscleman.

clue.text: Present is source of expectation? Certainly not!

parts.note: the present is now
taken as written

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of expectation

explanation.surface: A wrapped gift raises hopes, only for the answer to be a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWISE is an old adverb meaning in no way.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means in no manner at all, the same emphatic denial as saying by no means.

clue.text: … strongly built, fit and determined

parts.note: to be fit is to be well
set on something means determined to do it

explanation.surface: Continuing 15-down: the heavy is burly, healthy and resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-set person has a sturdy, solidly proportioned frame, firmly knit and powerfully made.

clue.text: Link between offices needs no metric conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into another form, so these letters are remade in a new order

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Communications between departments manage without switching to metres and kilos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metric conversion' reads as changing imperial measures, but conversion only signals the reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an internal telephone or speaker system letting people in different rooms of a building talk to each other.

clue.text: Sarcastic piece taken from The Scotsman, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wounding, sharply hurtful in remark

definitions.text: piece taken from The Scotsman, say
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an article clipped out of a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is the Edinburgh newspaper that set this puzzle; 'say' marks it as one example of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes remarks that wound, and also names an article clipped from a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Solid-looking cattle with last of tasty …

parts.note: farm animals collectively are livestock, or stock

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of tasty

explanation.surface: Beefy-looking cattle, the sentence running on into 23-down about tasty meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky person or animal is short and sturdily built, looking thickset and solid.

clue.text: To do with embassy's downgrading

parts.note: re means regarding, to do with
a legation is a diplomatic mission, a kind of embassy

explanation.surface: A diplomatic mission suffers a cut in its status.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition. In football, relegation is dropping to a lower division.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is moving someone or something down to a lower rank, class or league.

clue.text: Aid for needlewoman in perpetuity

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the next word, sitting within it

parts.note: the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Help for a seamstress that will last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: This small decorative case holds needles, pins and thread, so it is a useful accessory for someone who sews.

clue.text: … meat for working party beginning to feed

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, as in a sewing bee

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of feed

explanation.surface: Continuing 20-down: tasty meat to feed a team of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working party' suggests a committee; a bee is a social gathering for shared work, like a quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is the flesh of cattle eaten as food, a common red meat.

clue.text: Worker in drug firm to examine child with nasty mites

indicators.note: nasty suggests something spoilt or turned bad, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: to research something is to examine it closely
CH is the standard abbreviation for child
the five letters of mites in a new order

explanation.surface: A pharmaceutical lab worker checks a youngster suffering from a nasty infestation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmaceutical companies employ scientists who investigate new compounds in the laboratory to develop medicines.

clue.text: Recorded heartless luxury in celebrated style

indicators.note: without a heart the word loses its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: noted means written down, recorded
the word as written, before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: Gutted luxury is set down in famous fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the whole middle UXUR from LUXURY leaves its first and last letters, L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means famous, so the adverb describes doing something in a famous or remarkable way.

clue.text: Someone fleeing asylum at end of course

parts.note: asylum is shelter or refuge

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one wanted

parts.note: the final letter of course

explanation.surface: A fugitive seeks asylum at the end of a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is a person who has escaped persecution or war in their homeland and sought safety elsewhere.
